And 3 
Counsel for Applicant :- Hom Narayan Awasthi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC read with Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

Subsequently, the statement of the victim was recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., wherein, she did not support the prosecution story and stated that she had gone out of her own freewill and had also performed court marriage.
She also stated that they stayed in Nepal.
In the medical, the age has been tentatively found to be around 17 years.
There is nothing prima faice on record to determined the correct age of the victim.

In the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.,
she disclosed her age as 20 years.

entities.text: Pawan Kumar Maurya vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

4. Considering the fact that the applicant is in custody since 15.05.2023 and prima facie, the victim has not supported the prosecution story and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
5. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Pawan Kumar Maurya be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.91 of 2023,
under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Malhipur, District Shrawasti on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
